title: Asset allocation
desc: Split money between stocks, bonds and cash by goal and time

cards.title: Who can take more risk?
cards.situation: Sam needs his money in 1 year for a house deposit. Tom won’t touch his for 25 years. Who can hold more in stocks?

options.feedback: If stocks fall 30% next year, Sam can’t wait. He needs the money anyway.

options.text: Tom: he has time to recover from falls
options.feedback: Time lets Tom sit through the falls. Sam’s money needs to be there next year.

options.text: Both the same: stocks are stocks
options.feedback: The stocks are the same, but the time isn’t. Tom can wait out a bad year; Sam can’t.

cards.work: Stocks have fallen 30–50% in bad years. A one-year goal has no time to wait for a recovery.
cards.added: Feedback for C written for the Academy

cards.title: Your split
cards.text: **[[asset-allocation|Asset allocation]]** is how you split money between stocks, bonds and cash. For most people it matters more than any single pick.

blocks.tip: An example split to learn from, not advice. The right split depends on your goal and time.

cards.title: Goal and time set the split
cards.text: The sooner you need the money, the less of it sits in stocks.

visual.label: Example splits: 1–2 years 40% bonds 60% cash; 5–10 years 50% stocks 40% bonds 10% cash; 20+ years 80% stocks 15% bonds 5% cash

cards.foot: Example splits for learning, not advice. More time usually means more room for stock swings.
cards.added: Board label “tap a goal”: built as ▶ Play (split rows aren’t tappable)

cards.title: Short-term money stays out
cards.text: Money you need in the next **2 to 3 years** doesn’t belong in stocks. A crash could hit right before you need it.

cards.title: Do the split
cards.q: You have $10,000 and an example split of 60% stocks, 30% bonds, 10% cash. How much goes into bonds?

options.feedback: $6,000 is the stock part. Bonds are 30%.
$1,000 is the cash part. Bonds are 30%.
That treats 30% as $30. Take 30% of the whole $10,000.

cards.added: Feedback for the options the board doesn’t show written for the Academy

cards.title: Biggest swings
cards.q: In a mix of stocks, bonds and cash, which part usually swings the most?

options.feedback: Stocks bring the most growth and the biggest swings.
Bond prices move, but usually far less than stocks. Stocks bring the most growth and the biggest swings.
Cash barely moves. It’s the safest part, with the lowest return.
They don’t. Cash barely moves, bonds move a little, and stocks swing the most.

cards.headline: You can split money by goal and time.
lines: Allocation: the split between stocks, bonds and cash.
Short goals need calm money. Long goals can take swings.
Money needed within 2–3 years stays out of stocks.
